findings.statement: the store is larger than the memory allowed to cache it
the default readahead does not amplify a random read
findings.detail: 8697724 device bytes per 100-byte value with the default advice against 14149 with MADV_RANDOM -- 86977.2x against 141.5x amplification. Measured from /proc/self/io with the page cache dropped first, so these are bytes the device was asked for and not bytes inferred from file size

findings.statement: telling the kernel a random read is random makes it faster
findings.detail: 5143 reads/s with MADV_RANDOM against 204 with the default (random vs default: greater 25.231x (p=0.0022, rel_iqr 5.2%/1.9%)). Major faults: 69086 against 28201 -- the proof that these passes were cold, and the count of times the engine stopped for the disk

notes: page cache dropped before every pass; read amplification measured from /proc/self/io rather than inferred. Both arms read the same file in the same process and differ only in ReadOptions::readahead
